source.publication: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form ND-1 instructions and tables)
source.section: PDF p.15 Line 14 (the retired member's benefits only); PDF p.16 Line 22 and PDF p.17 qualified income; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 150,000.00 + military retirement (person 1) 40,000.00 = 190,000.00. Federal taxable income = 190,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 158,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 158,500.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 158,500.00. Subtractions: line 14 military retirement benefit exclusion 40,000.00. Line 17 total subtractions = 40,000.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 158,500.00 - 40,000.00 = 118,500.00. Line 19 = 118,500.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (118,500.00 - 80,975.00) = 1.95% x 37,525.00 = 731.7375, to the cent 731.74; taxable income is 100,000 or more, so the form itself uses the schedule (PDF p.29). Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: qualified income after lines 8 and 15 is 150,000.00 and 40,000.00; the lower is not more than 47,550.00, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 731.74. Only the spouse with military benefits (person 1) gets the exclusion; person 0's private pension stays taxed. Military retirement is not taken out of qualified income: the form reduces it only by lines 8 and 15.
